study.question: Does the validation advantage of recent-fine temporal compression survive when empty summaries are excluded from the shared target/history scorer normalization population? Observed limitation: g2-r0010-recent10 click AUC=0.6626241153 versus equal10=0.6605926365, early10=0.6602366530 and full100=0.6597487028; recent/equal have identical parameters and nearly equal batch inference p50 (12.581/12.517 ms). Yet candidate.py scores all thirty summary rows, including zero-count summaries whose interactions still contain the target, before discarding their zero-mass outputs. Pinned Dice normalizes across those rows. Thus a partition changes normalization exposure as well as centroid information. This confound is established by source inspection, not yet a measured explanation of the AUC difference.
study.hypothesis: Some of the recent-fine advantage is caused by the partition-dependent population of empty target-conditioned summary rows entering Dice/BatchNorm. Compacting only positive-count summaries before every existing scorer layer should remove this pathway and reduce the recent/equal performance gap. Each occupied summary receives one unit of normalization weight; pooling still uses exact original event counts. This does not equate the distributions or multiplicities of occupied summaries and does not assume that recency itself is irrelevant. The candidate may improve or worsen absolute AUC; this is a discriminating normalization/representation experiment, not a promised optimization.

nearest_work.difference: Archived primary text lines317-335 defines Dice using minibatch moments at training and moving moments at inference; inherited target-conditioned local activation and Dice are prior work. We change only which compressed summary rows enter the existing scorer population. This is a masking-aware adaptation with no priority/novelty claim. Pinned framework activations.py lines25-34 and baseline_reference.py were inspected.

Pinned benchmark implementation lines146-170 separates recent and earlier history and lines190-237 builds fixed and feature-conditioned query summaries before heterogeneous mixing. Our partition is inherited fixed mean compression; the new intervention is exclusion of empty rows from the inherited Dice scorer. No learned query or mixer is adopted. Original-author equivalence and originality remain unverified.

Pinned benchmark source lines174-225 uses LayerNorm, grouped InnerTrans and recent queries; lines229-272 shows local attention followed by learned compression. We keep simple count-weighted centroids and the existing target-conditioned scorer, and isolate a batch-population confound. LONGER is a nearest compression architecture, not a local effectiveness result; paper:longer resolves a paper link only, so no original-paper reproduction or novelty claim is made.

study.proposed_difference: Introduce PopulationScorer, an nn.Sequential subclass with the same child modules, parameter names, buffer names and construction order. In dense cells it delegates directly to the inherited Sequential. In occupied cells, positive-count summary indices compact the scorer input before any layer; scores scatter back into the original thirty-slot layout with zero for empty rows. This uses native BatchNorm statistics and variance conventions, with unchanged epsilon/momentum and unchanged tower normalization. Auxiliary functional_call receives the identical occupancy mask and isolated buffer copies. Training zero-row calls produce zero scorer contributions without state updates; a defensive one-row call uses existing running statistics without state updates. At inference native running-stat evaluation is used and auxiliary readout reuses the single primary pass. No count sidecar, loss change, extra parameters, router or private embedding bank is introduced. Boolean compaction may reduce scorer FLOPs but introduces dynamic indexing and GPU synchronization; no efficiency benefit is assumed.
predictions: Dense recent/equal controls reproduce the prior operators and, subject to host numerical nondeterminism, prior AUCs. A substantive replay discrepancy blocks causal interpretation until investigated; it is not evidence for normalization.

For a fixed initialized scorer and fixed occupied input rows, arbitrary finite changes to inactive interaction rows leave occupied-mode outputs, occupied-input gradients and persistent Dice updates unchanged in training. Dense normalization can change these quantities. This is an operator diagnostic, not an AUC result.

Let D_dense=AUC(recent_dense)-AUC(equal_dense), D_occupied=AUC(recent_occupied)-AUC(equal_occupied), and I=D_occupied-D_dense. Under the proposed major-confound hypothesis, I<0 and the positive recent/equal gap shrinks by at least half relative to D_dense (historical D_dense=0.0020314788). These are descriptive predeclared thresholds, not significance tests.

Analyze all four task AUC/Logloss, auxiliary-only mean and primary click selection separately. Historical recent10 auxiliary AUCs 0.701051/0.727912/0.666756 remain far below baseline 0.849070/0.864897/0.870182. This normalization study does not establish a remedy for that tradeoff.

Report paired recent/equal differences on frozen history bins empty,1-16,17-64,>64 with sample/positive/negative counts. Mixed-batch normalization can affect even empty-history predictions indirectly through training, so such slices are diagnostics, not local information-retention proofs.
falsifiers: Any occupied-mode dependence on inactive interaction values or any unexpected auxiliary updates to persistent scorer buffers/blocked parameters is an implementation failure. Stop before training; do not label it scientific counterevidence.

If the positive recent/equal gap persists within 0.0003 AUC of D_dense after occupancy masking, with valid replay controls, the claim that empty-row normalization explains a consequential portion is unsupported in this recipe. A larger occupied gap contradicts the predicted direction.

If I is negative but driven solely by recent_occupied collapsing, with no useful absolute quality/cost tradeoff, record the confound evidence separately from candidate utility; do not claim a better model.

If differences fail later paired-seed repetition or cannot be separated from compaction/numerical effects, retain only preliminary observations; a single-seed interaction does not establish a mechanism.
alternative_explanations: Actual recency-dependent information retention and regularization can explain the partition effect independently of empty rows; occupied centroids still differ in value distributions and duplicate strata.

Removing empty rows changes effective BatchNorm sample size and running-stat estimation as well as nuisance target copies. The intervention identifies this combined population pathway, not a unique reason for it.

BF16 reduction/kernel ordering, dynamic compaction, batch-dependent gradients, shared context updates and dense gradient clipping can alter trajectories even with identical parameter counts and initialization.
Multiple comparisons and the single frozen seed can favor a partition by chance. Dense replays at that same seed are consistency checks, not repetition.

Earlier branches show limitations rather than a clean novelty story: g2-r0000-match20 did not beat uniform10; g2-r0001-feedback_action and g2-r0002-uniform_feedback hurt click, selective gradients in g2-r0003-both_blocked and g2-r0004-context_only recovered it. g2-r0005-private_residual improved auxiliary tasks but cost435s and click0.660099 below context_only0.660647. g2-r0006-exact_blocked recovered auxiliary AUCs around0.793-0.796 without a click improvement. g2-r0007 aligned/rotated and g2-r0008 encode/pool alternatives supplied no convincing click advantage; g2-r0009-target10=0.659840 trailed history10=0.660052. These null/negative trajectories motivate checking an inherited confound instead of adding another router.
Offline feedback maturity and category/brand auxiliary label semantics remain frozen benchmark limitations; this study makes no production point-in-time claim.
